decisions.summary: A unit's code fingerprint takes the constants it names resolved only through its module's own constants and `from X import NAME` imports
decisions.why: FR-004 fingerprints the values of the in-scope module constants the unit NAMES, and US3 scenario 2 / SC-002 require every reader of a changed constant to be owed. A read through a module binding (`from . import law` then `law.JOIN_TOL`) names the constant but is not resolved by D3 or by the draft claims.py `values()` (Name nodes only). Observed 2026-10-02 by grep over the in-scope trees: 36 `law.<UPPER>` reads in hamletgen/ways alone (JOIN_TOL 12, DOORSTEP_MAX 7, DOORSTEP_FT 5, ...), whose readers would not be owed when that value changes. Fix: resolve `<alias>.<NAME>` where the alias is bound to an in-scope module (`from . import m`, `import ... as m`).

decisions.summary: Index verdict set is IN-STEP, DRIFTED, NEEDS-RESEARCH, MISLABELED, CANNOT-TELL; D7's refusing set lists the same four findings
decisions.why: FR-005 has six verdicts including UNCLAIMED, and FR-010 refuses every introduced FINDING, UNCLAIMED included (US4: 'unclaimed or undecided'). Dropping UNCLAIMED from the index and from D7's set removes a verdict and a refusal the accepted spec carries. Fix: add UNCLAIMED to D5's verdicts and to D7's refusing set.

decisions.summary: record writes VERDICT rows; UNCLAIMED lines are printed back for the session to write a claim, not recorded
decisions.why: FR-009: an UNCLAIMED finding 'is recorded as a row of its own on the unit (its label is the decision the check named); it stays a finding until a claim covering the decision is written and checked'; US3 scenario 4: 'it is recorded as needing a claim'. Printing it back leaves it in no index, which is the very state the spec's UNCLAIMED row exists to prevent. Fix: record an UNCLAIMED row keyed <path>::<qualname>#<decision>, dropped when a covering claim is checked.

decisions.summary: 'Changed the code' asked across keys: a unit whose core matches the core of any unit at the base is pre-existing, 'so a move or a rename with its code intact is pre-existing'
decisions.why: The mechanism does not reach the stated purpose. D3's core is ast.dump of the def/class/Assign node, which includes the unit's own name (draft claims.py `_dump(node)` on the FunctionDef / ClassDef / Assign), so a RENAMED unit's core matches nothing at the base and its first finding is refused - against FR-010, which names 'a unit merely renamed, whose code is unchanged under its new key' as PRE-EXISTING. Separately, matching ANY base unit lets a copy (same name and body newly added in a second module while the original stays) pass as pre-existing, though the delta created it. Fix: compare a name-stripped core for the cross-key test, and count only a match against a base unit whose key is gone at the head. (Aside: the constant-value hits carry the defining module's path, so a file split that moves a constant changes its readers' cores without changing a value - check this against the split work.)

decisions.summary: NEEDS-RESEARCH findings from the audit 'stand in the index' with DRIFTED, not corrected
decisions.why: FR-013: 'the claims are corrected (written, relabeled, an unresearched decision labeled UNRESEARCHED), and a DRIFTED finding stays in the index' - DRIFTED is the only finding the spec leaves standing; US6 likewise. A NEEDS-RESEARCH finding is by FR-005's definition a decision the record does not cover whose claim does not say unresearched, i.e. exactly the claim FR-013 says to relabel UNRESEARCHED (which also puts it on the report's open-research list, US6 scenario 2). Fix: treat NEEDS-RESEARCH like MISLABELED in the audit - relabel UNRESEARCHED and re-check within the same two rounds.
